correctness.rationale: For a,b>0 and 0<u,v<1, every admissible second phase is one of finitely many zeta=k*pi+theta or zeta=(k+1)*pi-theta; substitution gives a strictly monotone inverse phase and the explicit positive root of (a/pi^2)x^2+c x-a=0. Only phase choices 0<zeta<=b*pi permit x approaching zero. Each such phase and each of two nonmerged first-phase branches contributes a/epsilon+O(1); all other phases contribute O(1). Exact Jacobian determinant -ab(1+pi^2/x^2)sin(2Theta)sin(2Phi) is nonzero at each interior target. The K_b(v) floor formula and b=1/2 threshold account for phase boundaries inclusive; a harmonic-series estimate proves O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)) transverse Wasserstein-1 convergence. All quantifiers and target-edge exclusions are explicit. The package checks/verify_inverse.py checked 270 cutoff enumerations by two methods and 21,424 regular inverse samples; those checks do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The source 2023 map was read in its mathematical-model/dynamical sections and conclusion. The closest same-map indexed published-finding corpus theorem counts fixed points and proves saddle multipliers near (0,0), not inverse solutions for arbitrary fixed interior targets. Its N(epsilon)=2a/epsilon fixed-point count does not imply the phase-dependent arbitrary-target coefficient 2a K_b(v), the all-target b=1/2 threshold, or the transverse atomic inverse-fiber law. An inverse-valence theorem for a cosine-flux Chialvo map addresses different equations and an unbounded positive quadrant; it cannot be instantiated to the present bounded source with reciprocal x-singularity. Searches of aliases and stronger coverage disclosed no exact covering statement; broader literature remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A broader unindexed theorem about oscillatory inverse fibers could imply the counting formula after model-specific reduction.
The priority comparison is best-knowledge rather than independent exhaustive scholarly review.

value.rationale: An explicit, physically bounded state domain for an established coupled chaotic map can have countably infinite regular one-step inverse fibers accumulating at the undefined boundary. The precise inverse multiplicity coefficient is a target-dependent phase staircase, with a sharp b=1/2 threshold for all interior targets and a finite atomic transverse limiting law. This clarifies backward-state ambiguity and distinguishes infinite valence without critical folds from familiar finite-fold noninvertible maps; it is a global classification of a natural invariant of the published map, not an arbitrary selected finite table or a renamed fixed-point census. It does not imply cryptographic weakness or forward asymptotics.
